messages.author: 0ee8ae7c0d185529
messages.subject: ordered =  vs.  ordered=names()
parts:
Hi all,

A student in my class noticed that if she runs the following line 

fitmi <- cfa.mi(PISAmiss.model,estimator="wlsmv", ordered=names(mice.imp),
              data=mice.imp)
lavTestLRT.mi(fitmi,pool.method="D2",pool.robust=TRUE)

she gets a chi-square statistic that is much lower than if she runs

fitmi <- cfa.mi(PISAmiss.model,estimator="wlsmv", ordered=mice.imp,
              data=mice.imp)
lavTestLRT.mi(fitmi,pool.method="D2",pool.robust=TRUE)

I was able to reproduce that problem.  Any idea why?

Thanks,

David

messages.author: bc810b1d0900407f
messages.subject: Re: ordered = vs. ordered=names()
parts:
According to the help page, the argument "ordered" expects either a character vector or a logical value (TRUE/FALSE).

https://rdrr.io/cran/lavaan/man/sem.html

In the first case, you can check the output of names(mice.imp), and see what it is. It should be a vector of names, but likely not the variable names you want to specify as ordered variables.

In the second case, it is unlikely that using 'mice.imp', which is the dataset, will work correctly. It may not yield an error or a warning, probably due to the way the object of `ordered` is converted to something which happens to be acceptable (e.g., a character vector or a logical value).

You can also use lavInspect(fitmi, "ordered") to see whether the variables treated as ordinal variables are indeed what you expect.

Hope this helps.

-- Shu Fai
